subject: history
title: Mao's China 1949-1976
welcome_lead: From the proclamation of the People's Republic to the Cultural Revolution, study Mao Zedong's transformation of China.
meta_desc: History Authoritarian States Adventure 3: rise and rule of Mao Zedong, the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution.
final_note: You have traced Mao's revolution and its costs. The People's Republic he founded continues to shape global politics.

concepts.def: State proclaimed by Mao Zedong on 1 October 1949 after victory in the Chinese Civil War.
Redistribution of land from landlords to peasants, accompanied by mass denunciations and executions.
Brief liberalisation followed by Anti-Rightist Campaign repressing critics.
Mass mobilisation policy of rapid industrialisation and communal agriculture causing mass famine.
Mao-led upheaval mobilising youthful Red Guards against perceived bourgeois elements within the CCP.
Compilation of Mao's quotations, distributed in hundreds of millions of copies during the Cultural Revolution.

walkthroughs.body_html: After defeating the Nationalist Guomindang in 1949, Mao consolidated power through land reform, intervention in the Korean War (1950-53), the Marriage Law (1950) and campaigns against 'counter-revolutionaries'. Soviet aid supported early Five-Year Plans focused on heavy industry.

From 1958 Mao replaced the cautious Soviet model with rapid collectivisation into people's communes, mass mobilisation for backyard steel furnaces and unrealistic production targets. Combined with bad weather, the policy produced a catastrophic famine in which an estimated 15-45 million people died.

Sidelined politically, Mao launched the Cultural Revolution in 1966 to attack 'capitalist roaders' such as Liu Shaoqi and Deng Xiaoping. Red Guards persecuted teachers, officials and 'class enemies' and destroyed cultural heritage. The chaos receded after Mao's death on 9 September 1976 and the arrest of the Gang of Four.
